description: Minimal graphs the property-based round trips (generative.ts) shrank a failure to. Each runs through every listed target as export -> import (bytes) -> compare under the target's documented losses. A case with knownFailure is an open bug and runs as an expected failure; the others are regressions of fixed bugs. Numbers JSON cannot spell are {"$num": "-0" | "Infinity" | "-Infinity" | "NaN"}.

cases.name: negative-zero-weight
cases.exercises: an explicit weight of -0 keeps its sign (was written as 0 by every weight formatter)

cases.name: negative-zero-cell
cases.exercises: an f64 cell of -0 next to a non-integral value keeps its sign (formatF64 and the JSON writer wrote 0)

cases.name: lone-negative-zero-column
cases.exercises: an f64 column holding only -0 is written -0.0 and must be widened to f64 on reading (the text writer believed the sink inferred f64 for -0; graph-format infers i32)

cases.name: json-integral-after-nonfinite
cases.exercises: an f64 column of [-0, NaN]: NaN is written as null, so the column reads back i32; check() must announce W_INTEGRAL_F64_AS_I32

cases.name: dot-backslash-newline
cases.exercises: a text holding a backslash before a line break is a Graphviz line continuation; export() must refuse it (E_DOT_TRAILING_BACKSLASH) rather than write a text that reads back without both characters

cases.name: csv-edgeless-undirected
cases.exercises: an undirected graph without edges has no Type cell to carry its direction; check() must announce W_CSV_DIRECTION_DROPPED

cases.name: pajek-numeric-text-parameter
cases.exercises: a string parameter holding -3 reads back as a number; check() must announce W_TEXT_INFERRED

cases.name: pajek-infinite-weight
cases.knownFailure: pajek: an infinite edge weight is written as `Infinity`, which the Pajek importer reads as a parameter name without a value (E_PAJEK_LINE) and drops the edge; check() announces nothing. Pajek has no spelling for infinity: check() should refuse or note it

cases.name: csv-one-column-node-table-pipe
cases.exercises: a node table with the Id column only, an id holding `|`
cases.knownFailure: csv: a one-column node table is written with a bare `|`, `;` or tab inside an id, and the importer's delimiter sniff picks that character, splitting the rows (E_CSV_FIELD_COUNT). The exporter should quote a cell holding any sniffable delimiter when the table has one column

cases.name: gml-list-marker-text
cases.knownFailure: gml: a text cell equal to NetworkX's list markers ("[]", "()", "_networkx_list_start") is written as that string and read back as a list; check() announces nothing. Either note it (the NetworkX convention makes the text ambiguous) or write such a text so it cannot be taken for a marker

cases.name: neo4j-tab-in-quoted-id
cases.exercises: an id holding tabs, on a node with three self-loops
cases.knownFailure: neo4j: the importer sniffs the delimiter; the one-column :ID section gives no evidence for the comma, the quoted ids' tabs repeat evenly, so the file is read tab-delimited and every relationship row fails (text after a closing quote). neo4j-admin uses a comma unless told otherwise
